Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Albuquerque NM
1221 AM MST Sat Nov 21 2026

...New SHORT TERM, LONG TERM, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Issued at 1218 AM MST Sat Nov 21 2026
 
- Another round of dense fog will impact travel in southeast New 
  Mexico tonight through Saturday morning.

- Two quick-hitting disturbances, the first Saturday and the
  second Monday evening into early Tuesday morning of next week,
  are forecast to bring light precipitation to northern New
  Mexico. Brief and localized slick travel with low visibility 
  may develop in the higher terrain.

- Coldest temperatures of the season thus far in many areas
  expected this weekend. Temperatures will remain near to slightly
  below normal through next week.

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Today through Sunday)
Issued at 1218 AM MST Sat Nov 21 2026

It'll be yet another foggy night in southeast New Mexico. Mist has 
developed and visibility will continue to fall through the night, 
although dissipation will likely occur earlier in the morning 
compared to the past few mornings as surface winds rotate around to 
the south and eventually southwest.

Meanwhile, a positively tilted trough is digging into the Four 
Corners region tonight. Cold air advection is already occurring aloft 
well ahead of the sfc front. The Pacific frontal boundary currently 
over eastern AZ is quite weak, but frontogenesis will start 
occurring tonight over the Continental Divide as the boundary aligns 
better with the right entrance region of the approaching jet streak. 
A brief period of snow is likely along I-40 during the morning as 
the temperature gradient intensifies. Given the marginal 
temperatures and brief nature of the snow, significant travel 
impacts are not expected. The frontal boundary will weaken as 
quickly as it strengthened as it moves westward down into the Rio 
Grande Valley. There should still be just enough strength for a 
quick burst of snow over the Jemez, Sangre de Cristo, and 
Sandia/Manzano Mountains, with generally less than 2" of 
accumulation. Southwest slopes along the Sangre de Cristo Mountains 
could have a little bit more with 90th percentile snowfall amounts 
suggesting up to 5" above 10,000 feet.

It will be a chilly afternoon in the western two-thirds of the state 
in the wake of the cold front and temperatures will continue to 
plummet overnight into Sunday morning. Winds should calm down enough 
for valley inversions to develop with a few northern mountain 
valleys dropping down into the single digits. High clouds will 
increase in coverage from the west through the day Sunday so 
temperatures have trended a few degrees lower. Highs will range from 
around 3 degrees below normal in the northern mountains to 15 
degrees below normal in the eastern plains.

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Sunday night through Friday)
Issued at 1218 AM MST Sat Nov 21 2026

Overall, the forecast next week is looking relatively dry with near 
average temperatures. Models are starting to get into slightly 
better agreement that a quick-hitting trough will traverse New 
Mexico on Monday. While ensemble guidance is trending further south, 
the bulk of precipitation will still remain north of the CO/NM 
border. The northern mountains should squeeze out a couple more 
inches of snow, but more than that looks unlikely given the speed at 
which this storm will be moving.

Ridging returns Tuesday of next week, but the progressive pattern 
continues as another quick-hitting trough starts to take shape late 
in the week. The ENS and GEPS continue to favor a faster-moving 
positively tilted trough that would bring nothing more than a dry 
cold front to New Mexico while the GEFS mean shows a neutrally 
tilted trough that could draw just enough moisture for some light 
rain/mountain snow. Agreement is high that ridging will amplify over 
the desert southwest late week into the weekend, but a strengthening 
Pacific jet will begin to break down the ridge early next week. It 
is unclear how soon that will translate to more unsettled weather 
over New Mexico, but long-term sub-seasonal guidance continues to 
point towards wetter and colder weather during the early part of 
December.

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS)
Issued at 1036 PM MST Fri Nov 20 2026

Fog has begun forming over southeast NM but with less coverage 
and duration at this time than recent nights. The probability of 
vsby <0.5 mile is still above 75% from near Clovis to Roswell and
points southeast. The focus will shift to a cold front surging 
into western NM before sunrise with a northwest wind shift and a 
period of MVFR rain and snow thru sunrise. This front will surge 
quickly east thru 2PM Saturday with a squall-like band of wind, 
rain, and snow over central NM. Clearing will occur from west 
to east thru sunset in the wake of the front. Rain/snow will 
impact northeast NM Saturday evening along with a northerly 
wind shift.

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1218 AM MST Sat Nov 21 2026

Critical fire weather conditions are not expected through the next 
seven days. A Pacific cold front will cross the state from west to 
east today, ushering in a colder and drier airmass. A brief period 
of rain and snow above 7,000 feet will occur with some minor (1-4") 
of snow accumulation in the northern mountains.

After dry and quiet weather Sunday, another quick-hitting storm 
system will send another Pacific front with light rain/mountain snow 
across New Mexico Monday into Monday night. Outside of a few 
stronger breezes across the northeast Sunday and Monday, winds will 
generally be light through the next seven days.

Ventilation today will be good to excellent due to the passage of a 
cold front, but poor to fair ventilation is likely to prevail in 
most areas through the end of next week.

&&
